# Files sub-actions

## Delete file

Deletes a file from your computer. Be careful: it is removed for good, not sent to the recycle bin.

| Setting | What to put in |
| --- | --- |
| **File** | The file's full location on your computer, like C:\Stream\old.txt. |
| **Fail if missing** | Tick to get an error if the file is not there. Unticked, nothing happens when it is missing. Starts as: `false`. |

**Variables it adds**

| Variable | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `%fileDeleted%` | True if the file existed and was deleted |

<small>Type id: `core.deleteFile`</small>

## File exists

Checks if a file or folder exists on your computer, then runs the True steps if it does or the False steps if it does not.

| Setting | What to put in |
| --- | --- |
| **File or folder** | The full location to look for, like C:\Stream\score.txt. |
| **Look for** | File = only count files. Folder = only count folders. Either = count both. Options: File, Folder, Either. Starts as: `File`. |

Paths it can take: **True**, **False**.

**Variables it adds**

| Variable | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `%fileExists%` | True if it was found |

<small>Type id: `core.fileExists`</small>

## Read file

Reads a whole text file and saves everything in it in a variable. Good for showing text another program wrote, like a song title file.

| Setting | What to put in |
| --- | --- |
| **File** | The file's full location on your computer, like C:\Stream\song.txt. |
| **Store in argument** | The variable that receives the text, without % signs. The default fileContent means you use %fileContent%. Starts as: `fileContent`. |

**Variables it adds**

| Variable | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `%fileContent%` | All the text in the file (the variable name can be changed in the settings) |

<small>Type id: `core.readFile`</small>

## Read lines from file

Reads a text file line by line. Every line gets its own variable: line0 is the first line, line1 the second, and so on.

| Setting | What to put in |
| --- | --- |
| **File** | The file's full location on your computer, like C:\Stream\list.txt. |
| **Store in argument** | The start of the variable names, without % signs. With the default line you get %line0%, %line1% and so on. Starts as: `line`. |
| **Parse variables** | Tick to replace any %variables% written inside the file with their values. Starts as: `false`. |
| **Attempt auto-typing** | Tick so a line that holds a number is stored as a real number. Untick if unsure. Starts as: `false`. |

**Variables it adds**

| Variable | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `%lineCount%` | How many lines the file has |
| `%line0%` | The first line (line1 is the second, and so on; the start of the name can be changed) |
| `%fileFound%` | True if the file was found |

<small>Type id: `core.readLines`</small>

## Read random line

Picks a random line from a text file and saves it in a variable. Great for a list of jokes, quotes or ideas that you keep in a plain file.

| Setting | What to put in |
| --- | --- |
| **File** | The file's full location on your computer, like C:\Stream\jokes.txt. |
| **Store in argument** | The variable that receives the line, without % signs. The default randomLine means you use %randomLine%. Starts as: `randomLine`. |
| **Skip empty lines** | Tick to never pick an empty line. Starts as: `true`. |
| **How many lines** | How many different lines to pick. With more than 1, the extra ones go in randomLine1, randomLine2, and so on. Starts as: `1`. |
| **Parse variables** | Tick to replace any %variables% written inside the line with their values. Starts as: `false`. |
| **Attempt auto-typing** | Tick so a line that holds a number is stored as a real number. Untick if unsure. Starts as: `false`. |

**Variables it adds**

| Variable | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `%randomLine%` | The picked line (the variable name can be changed in the settings) |
| `%lineNumber%` | Which line of the file it was, starting at 1 |
| `%lineCount%` | How many lines the file could choose from |
| `%fileFound%` | True if the file was found |

<small>Type id: `core.readRandomLine`</small>

## Read specific line from file

Reads one chosen line of a text file, for example line 3, and saves it in a variable.

| Setting | What to put in |
| --- | --- |
| **File** | The file's full location on your computer, like C:\Stream\list.txt. |
| **Store in argument** | The variable that receives the line, without % signs. The default line means you use %line%. Starts as: `line`. |
| **Line number (from 1)** | Which line to read. 1 = the first line. If the file is shorter, you get an empty value. Starts as: `1`. |
| **Parse variables** | Tick to replace any %variables% written inside the line with their values. Starts as: `false`. |
| **Attempt auto-typing** | Tick so a line that holds a number is stored as a real number. Untick if unsure. Starts as: `false`. |

**Variables it adds**

| Variable | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `%line%` | The line that was read (the variable name can be changed in the settings) |
| `%lineCount%` | How many lines the file has |
| `%fileFound%` | True if the file was found |

<small>Type id: `core.readSpecificLine`</small>

## Write file

Writes text into a file on your computer, adding to the end or replacing everything. Good for feeding a text source in OBS, like a follower goal.

| Setting | What to put in |
| --- | --- |
| **File** | The file's full location, like C:\Stream\goal.txt. Cuebot creates the file if it is missing. |
| **Text** | The text to write. You can use %variables%, like "Latest follower: %user%". |
| **Mode** | Append = add to the end of the file. Overwrite = erase the file and write only this text. Options: Append, Overwrite. Starts as: `Append`. |
| **End with a new line** | Tick to finish the text with a line break, so the next write starts on a new line. Starts as: `true`. |
| **Create missing folders** | Tick to create the folders on the way if they do not exist yet. Starts as: `true`. |

<small>Type id: `core.writeFile`</small>
